‘Stick’ Season 2 Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Come Out?
Another round of competitive golf will be served up in Season 2 of Apple TV ’s Stick starring Owen Wilson and Peter Dager.
The golf comedy, which also stars Lilli Kay, Mariana Treviño, Marc Maron, Timothy Olyphant and Judy Greer, will see Pluribus star Rhea Seehorn join the second season in a new series regular role.
Owen Wilson’s Pryce Cahill Makes Play At U.S. Open In ‘Stick’ Season 2 Trailer
Rex Linn, Sasha Alexander & Missi Pyle Join Apple TV’s ‘Stick’ For Season 2
For the full Stick Season 2 release schedule, see details below.
The second season of Stick will premiere on Apple TV Wednesday, November 4. Watch on Deadline
Season 2 will have ten episodes that roll out right before the end of the year. After the first two premiere on November 4, one new episode per week will arrive on Wednesdays through December 30, 2026.
Owen Wilson stars as down on his luck former professional golfer Pryce Cahill, who took young Santiago Wheeler (Peter Dager) under his wing in Season 1 and coached the golf phenom. Mariana Treviño portrays Santi’s mother Elena, and Marc Maron portrays one of Pryce’s oldest friends and former golf gaddies, Mitts. Lilli Key portrays Zero, a friend and then more to Santi who sees what he’s going through at a golf tournament in Season 1.
RELATED: ‘Stick’ Creator Jason Keller Talks Crafting Heart, Casting Peter Dager And Exploring Pryce’s Past In Season 2
Timothy Olyphant and Judy Greer have been promoted to series regulars in their respective roles of Clark Ross, former rival of Pryce’s and Pryce’s ex-wife Amber-Linn.
Season 2 has some new faces in Pluribus Emmy winner Rhea Seehorn, who will portray Coach Amanda. Saturday Night Live alum John Higgins has joined the new season, as have Rex Linn, Sasha Alexander and Missi Pyle . Billy Zane will also recur in Season 2 .
In the second season of the golf comedy, Pryce will bet on himself and take a shot at the U.S. Open. Santi faces leveling up in his professional golf career, meaning his talent becomes expected on a consistent basis, which changes the sport for him.
